sections.content: How many people stayed in Salford after gaining qualifications?

Salford is a large town in the North West. Salford also has a university.

Salford has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Salford ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 3,720 state-school pupils from Salford who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 855 (23%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,185 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Salford to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Salford's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Salford in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Salford move to?

Of Salford's graduates, 270 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 150 of those graduates (56%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Salford's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 300 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 230 of those qualified non-graduates (77%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Salford's GCSE cohort:

  • 100 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 50 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 78% of graduates and 47% of qualified non-graduates living in Salford had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,585 graduates and 1,625 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Salford. This is compared with the 855 graduates and 1,185 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 22% of the graduates had also lived in Salford as GCSE pupils, while 78% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Salford in 2018 to 2019, 53% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 47% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
